title: Drama work as a sustained sequence
statement: Run drama-based literacy work as a sustained, guided sequence over several hours rather than a single task, since its measured effects are larger that way.
example: A meta-analysis of 42 reports and 200+ effect sizes found larger effects when the work was teacher-led over multiple hours.
detail: Notes on a proposed student performance task found most support for performance pedagogy institutional or self-reported, and named as the strongest evidence a meta-analysis of 30 years of research on drama-based pedagogies and K-12 literacy outcomes: 42 reports, 200+ effect sizes and a significant positive effect on achievement, attitude and motivation, larger when teacher-led over multiple hours than as a single task (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/video-04-student-performance-gallery.md`, lines 15-30). A Readers' Theatre meta-analysis of 11 studies with ages 6-12 found a large effect on reading skills (lines 30-33). The notes therefore made a one-off performance task an optional extension that earns a bigger role over several lessons (lines 99-101).
against: "No Shakespeare-specific or Grade-9-specific trial of a filmed-performance-gallery task was found." (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/video-04-student-performance-gallery.md`, line 128), and the Readers' Theatre evidence is elementary-age, so transfer to Grade 9 is an inference (lines 31-33).

evidence.quote: significant positive effect on achievement/attitude/motivation, **larger when teacher-led over multiple hours, not a single task** — strength: **meta-analysis** ([ERIC](https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1275486)).
favors sustained, repeated performance practice over a single one-off task
